newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mondale hopeful US, Japan will solve insurance spat.
newsitem.headline: Mondale hopeful US, Japan will solve insurance spat.

text.p: Outgoing U.S. ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale said on Tuesday he was "hopeful" that the United States and Japan would solve a dispute over Japan's insurance market by a December 15 deadline.
"I'm hopeful we're going to have an agreement, but I would also tell you that I don't know why," Mondale told a news conference.

He said U.S. and Japanese negotiators had a history of settling trade feuds at the last minute "on the court steps" and added: "I think both countries know it's important to get this thing resolved, so I will say I'm optimistic."

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka will meet here on December 6-7 to try to settle the dispute ahead of the deadline. Both sides have said the talks are probably the last chance the ministers would have to meet before the December 15 deadline.

The dispute, which has become a major irritant in U.S.-Japan trade ties, centres on U.S. charges that Japan is poised to renege on a 1994 pact on deregulation of its $400 billion insurance market by opening up a niche market dominated by U.S. insurers before deregulating its primary life and non-life insurance sectors.
